title: Blessed Redeemer How Divine
description: Blessed Redeemer How Divine in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 38, headed “[Supplement.] The universal law of equity. Matt. 8. 12”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Long Metre (8.8.8.8). This page sets the words to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Bless-ed Re-deem-er how di-vine, How right-eous is this rule of thine, "To do to all men just the same "As we ex-pect or wish from them."

lines: How righteous is this rule of thine,
"To do to all men just the same
"As we expect or wish from them."
This golden lesson, short and plain,
Gives not the mind nor memory pain;
How blest would every nation be,
Thus rul'd by love and equity!
All would be friends without a foe,
Jesus, forgive us, that we keep
Thy sacred law of love asleep,
No more let envy, wrath, and pride,
But thy blest maxims be our guide.

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
